inputs.root_cause: safetensors' last unresolved obligation (SAL-SAFETENSORS-OBL-9229B611B9CCD5F8, bidirectional interop against the official release plus collision-free coinstall) was marked GAP-002-environment-blocked in the shared dev venv: 4 tests fail there with importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError for 'safetensors' since the official PyPI package was never installed.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-SAFETENSORS-OBL-9229B611B9CCD5F8 (SAFETENSORS-INTEROP-001), safetensors' only remaining unresolved obligation.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: All 4 previously-failing interop tests genuinely pass end-to-end in a real, isolated, reproducible wheel-install environment (tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format safetensors's ephemeral proof venv, plus the official safetensors package installed into that same venv). One genuine bug found and fixed in the test file itself along the way.
inputs.regression_tier: full safetensors package suite (tests/python/safetensors), confirmed clean in the shared dev venv both before and after this investigation

execution_steps: 1. Investigated the exact GAP-002 mechanism precisely rather than trusting the existing missing_behavior description at face value (per GAP-008). Confirmed format-factory-safetensors and safetensors are DIFFERENT importlib.metadata distribution names -- no metadata-name collision between them as such. The actual, simpler cause: the official safetensors PyPI package was never installed in the shared dev venv at all.

2. Tried the obvious fix: added safetensors>=0.4 to pyproject.toml's dev extras and pip installed it into .venv. 2 of the 4 target tests passed immediately; the other 2 (which specifically assert format_factory.safetensors resolves under site-packages, i.e. a real wheel install, not editable) failed as expected -- editable installs never satisfy that assertion, matching the missing_behavior's own note that this needs an isolated wheel-install environment.

3. Before proceeding further, ran the FULL safetensors suite in the shared dev venv and discovered a real regression: 7 collection errors in test_safetensors_validation.py and 6 sibling files, all importing a bare top-level safetensors.exceptions/safetensors.safetensors_codec module. Confirmed causality directly: uninstalling the official package made these pass again immediately. This is a genuine, unrelated legacy shadow-package test suite in this same directory that needs a DIFFERENT local 'safetensors' module identity, which the official PyPI package's presence shadows/conflicts with in the shared venv.

4. Reverted both the pyproject.toml dev-dependency addition and the .venv pip install completely, confirming the shared dev venv suite returned to its exact original baseline (403 passed, 1 skipped, the same 4 pre-existing failures) before proceeding -- the shared dev venv must NOT carry the official safetensors package.

5. Used the already-existing, purpose-built tools/run_package_install_proof.py --format safetensors instead: it builds format-factory-safetensors as a real wheel and installs it into a genuinely isolated, ephemeral proof venv (.local/package-install-proof-venv, gitignored) with no shadow-package test suite present. Installed the official safetensors package into that SAME isolated venv (no conflict there, since the legacy shadow tests are never run against it) and ran the 4 target tests directly against it with that venv's own pytest.

6. 3 of 4 passed immediately; the 4th (test_preservation_roundtrip_is_officially_readable) failed on a real, distinct logic assertion, not an environment issue: it assumed 'absent __metadata__' and 'explicitly empty __metadata__: {}' are semantically equivalent and should both round-trip to no __metadata__ key. Read reader.py's _decode_header, whose own docstring explicitly documents SAFETENSORS-PRESERVE-001 requires distinguishing these two states -- confirming the SOURCE behavior (writing __metadata__: {} for an explicitly-declared-but-empty case) is correct and the TEST's assumption was the bug. Fixed the test's assertion to expect the documented distinction instead of collapsing it.

7. Re-ran all 4 tests against the isolated proof venv: all 4 passed. Ran ruff on the one changed test file (clean). Re-ran the full safetensors suite in the shared dev venv once more to confirm zero lingering state from the venv churn (still 403 passed, 1 skipped, same 4 known failures there by design).
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/safetensors/ -q -- 403 passed, 1 skipped, 4 failed (same 4 known environment-scoped failures, unchanged baseline)
